metadata.scenario_context: Jacob is having difficulties in his Economics class and he needs additional help from his professor. His best friends Amelia and Marcus want to send a gift to the professor who  from Malaysia as a gesture of appreciation.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Hong Kong SAR strongly agree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss choosing a gift made from leather for Jacob.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the possibility of paying a bribe to teachers for better service.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what kind of gift to give to Jacob's professor.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the possibility of paying a bribe to teachers for better service.

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message: Hey Amelia, have you thought about getting Jacob's professor a leather gift? I think something like a leather notebook or a wallet could be really nice. It shows appreciation but also has that personal touch. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Amelia
shared_prefix.message: A leather gift sounds nice, but we should consider something that reflects his culture too. Maybe a traditional Malaysian craft or something local? It could really show our appreciation. I just think a leather item might be a bit too common. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message: I get that, but leather has a certain elegance that fits well in academia. Plus, it’s practical. I think it says more than just 'common.' But if we want to include something cultural, we could pair it with a leather item. Also, just out of curiosity... do you think it's okay to pay teachers for better service? I mean, it feels wrong to me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Amelia
shared_prefix.message: I see what you mean about the elegance, pairing it with something cultural could work. But we really need to avoid anything that feels like a bribe. Paying teachers for better service is definitely not right. It undermines their role and sends the wrong message. We should focus on genuine appreciation instead. What about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message: I agree it’s good to show genuine appreciation, but I think we should be careful about assuming teachers always deliver great service without any incentive. In my experience, this can be different in various places. I really don’t think it’s right to pay teachers for better service. It just... it feels wrong to me. But let’s focus on finding that perfect leather gift and maybe a cultural piece to go with it. What else do you think we could consider?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Amelia
shared_prefix.message: I don’t know about that. At the end of the day, it’s all the same. People figure it out in different ways, and I think we just need to focus on what we can give Jacob’s professor that he’ll appreciate. Maybe we can look into a nice leather gift and add a cultural element to it. I’m sure we can find the right balance without getting too caught up in the details. What do you think fits best?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
